Since the conversion between Celsius and Fahrenheit is different from that in the ThinQ app, we implemented it to retrieve the appropriate temperature settings(min, max) and state values ​​in hass.config.unit.
There were many issues raised by users regarding this, and this PR must be merged in order to properly retrieve data for each unit of the entire device.

Please review for this. (added tests when hass.config.unit is Fahrenheit)

@Jelloitsalive12 Thank you for your report.
ThinQ Connect only provides Celsius and Home Assistant is converting it to Fahrenheit.
ThinQ app shows differences in temperature due to different Fahrenheit conversion standards.
ThinQ Connect is improving this issue.

review_comments: why is this call required? as long as we set the correct "source" unit on the climate entity, HA should take care of converting it to the correct "destination" unit that the user selected.

Among ThinQ devices, there are devices that have a Celsius/Fahrenheit conversion map, and in many cases, **the result is different from the conversion result from HA.** 
Therefore, to get the unit map (min, max, step) environment for a device that matches the HA configuration unit, the integration must set the current settings to the preferred temperature units. 
[mismatch issue](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/130073)
